title: A short reflection and a tester who's done talking: no dragging it out, straight to the next step
origin: Issue #77 (proof plus reflection): Should, follow-ups never forced

history.text: Starts in 10, Theo! 3 sets of 8 push-ups and 12 squats in the living room at 6:30.

plan.step: 3 sets of 6 push-ups and 10 squats in the living room
plan.proof_note: a quick voice note saying what you did
plan.reason: Short sets every day build the base before anything harder.

step_days.step: 3 sets of 6 push-ups and 10 squats in the living room
3 sets of 7 push-ups and 10 squats in the living room

today_step.step: 3 sets of 8 push-ups and 12 squats in the living room at 6:30 pm (about 15 min)

testerLines: [voice: Done, three sets of eight push-ups and twelve squats.]
it was fine, legs were tired on the last set
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: ZOH shouldn't keep a tester talking for its own sake.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH counts the voice note, celebrates and asks once for a quick reflection (a voice note is easiest). After "legs were tired on the last set" it may ask at most one short, specific follow-up; after "nah that's it" it stops digging and proposes the next step day's step, fully defined (what, where, when, how long), sensibly not a big jump given tired legs, and asks if it works. After "let's go" it confirms in one line with no new question.
